name: Sardonyx
emotional: Builds a strong sense of self
physical: Traditionally linked to stamina and steady energy
Associated with a sense of physical confidence
Often worn for general feelings of strength
summary: Sardonyx is the banded blend of red carnelian and white onyx, long worn for courage, integrity and protection. Explore its lore, uses and care.
intro: Sardonyx is a banded chalcedony in which layers of reddish sard (carnelian) alternate with white or black onyx. The result is a striped stone in rust, brick, cream and sometimes chocolate brown that looks like a tiny sedimentary cliff. Because the layers have different colors and textures, it is ideal for carving, which is why you often meet it as cameos and intaglio rings. Tumbled pieces show soft stripes that feel earthy and friendly. It is inexpensive, hard-wearing and the traditional August birthstone alongside peridot and spinel.
history: The name joins sard, a reddish stone named after the city of Sardis, with onyx. Roman craftsmen loved it for cameos, cutting the white bands into raised figures against the red ground. Soldiers are said to have worn sardonyx engraved with gods of war, hoping to gain courage in battle. Medieval writers listed it among the stones of the high priest's breastplate and the foundations of the Heavenly Jerusalem in the Book of Revelation. Today the gem is mined mostly in India and Brazil, and much material is dyed to boost the stripe contrast.
meaning: Sardonyx has long been called the stone of honesty and strong character. Healers describe it as combining the fire of carnelian with the steadiness of onyx, so it supports action that is both bold and disciplined. People use it for courage in public speaking, for keeping promises, and for protecting friendships and marriages from careless words. Traditionally it is seen as a stone of stamina and good cheer, helping you keep going without burning out. It is linked to the root and solar plexus chakras, making it a good partner when you want confidence that rests on a solid base. If you feel pulled between impulse and caution, many people say this stone helps hold the middle.
howToUse: Wear sardonyx as a ring or pendant when you need to project calm authority. Hold a piece in your dominant hand while stating a goal aloud, then keep it in your pocket as a reminder. Place a stone on a desk to support steady work habits, or give a small tumbled stone to a friend as a token of loyalty. In meditation rest it at the base of the spine and picture a warm red-brown light rooting you downward. Its banding makes it a nice worry stone for thumbs.
care: Sardonyx is tough and handles lukewarm water, so rinse it freely and dry with a soft cloth. Cleanse by smoke, sound, moonlight or a rest on selenite. Direct sun is fine for natural pieces, but dyed ones can fade over years, so limit exposure for those. Store it apart from harder gems and in a soft pouch so the polish stays bright. Avoid ultrasonic cleaners for carved or fractured pieces.
identify: Look for straight, parallel bands of red-brown and white, with a waxy luster and cool touch. Glass fakes show swirls, bubbles or an unnaturally perfect pattern. Dyed agate is common, so strong color concentrated in cracks suggests staining. Layered cameo fakes made of resin or shell can be spotted by weight and warmth in the hand. True sardonyx is chalcedony, so it will scratch glass with ease.

faq.a: Sardonyx stands for courage, integrity and protection. Crystal healers link it to the root and solar plexus chakras and use it to support honest speech, loyalty and steady confidence.

faq.q: Is sardonyx the same as onyx?
faq.a: They are close relatives. Both are banded chalcedony, but onyx has black and white bands while sardonyx has reddish-brown sard layers alternating with white. The reddish layers give sardonyx its warmer, earthier look.
Yes. Sardonyx is a traditional August birthstone, listed with peridot and spinel. It is also the traditional gift for a seventh wedding anniversary in some lists.
